spike_verdict: The core tension (2022 council report nearly revoked a 36-year-old status, 92% of ~4,000 backed keeping it, promised safety upgrades unfulfilled as of Oct 2023) is fully carried by the evidence, but the page overstates finality ('never came') where the record only supports 'hadn't come by Oct 2023.'

blocking.claim: A 2022 council report on drugs and syringes nearly ended Melbourne's only legal nudist beach; 92% of 4,000 said keep it, but the fixes never came.
blocking.problem: 'Never came' asserts a permanent, closed-out fact. The fact sheet's own dead_ends explicitly say: 'Current (2024-2026) status... and whether the promised car-park cameras, signage and access-track repairs were ever delivered after October 2023 - no source in this bundle covers anything past Oct 2023.' The sheet's own spike_candidate wording (which the page should have kept) correctly bounded this to '...stayed unmet by 2023,' not 'never.' showcase.json's spike_explainer and honest_reckoning_note get this right ('at least not by the last date this record covers'); only the headline spike_statement overstates it.
blocking.evidence: research/sunnyside-beach-3.json dead_ends[0]; spike_candidates[0].statement ('...stayed unmet by 2023'); F29 (MPNews, Oct 2023, quote: 'no evidence... of any progress in any of these areas, but of course, it could still be in the planning stage')
blocking.fix: Replace 'but the fixes never came' with 'but the fixes still hadn't come by late 2023' (or equivalent phrasing that scopes the claim to the record's actual end date, matching showcase.json's honest_reckoning_note).

blocking.where: culture.mdx, section 'What the Numbers Actually Show', final paragraph
blocking.claim: As of October 2023, the people who had organized the online campaign to save the beach were the same people reporting, on the record, that none of the promised upgrades had shown up.
blocking.problem: Misattribution. I fetched the MPNews Oct 2023 source (F13/F14/F28/F29) directly: the person reporting no progress is named 'Michael James, the Victorian representative on the Australian Naturist Federation' and 'James, who has been going to Sunnyside North for about 30 years' - he is NOT described in the article as an organizer of the Facebook group or the change.org petition. Those were run by 'Michael' (25+ year regular, gay, called the vote result 'emotional' per F26) - a different person the page itself elsewhere carefully distinguishes ('different petitions, on different platforms, run by people who happen to share a first name'). Michael James is, per the ledger, the man behind the minor gopetition.com petition (11 signatures, F21) - not 'the people who had organized the online campaign.' showcase.json's parallel passage avoids this error by calling him only 'a regular beachgoer.'
blocking.evidence: https://www.mpnews.com.au/2023/10/25/no-easy-access-to-nude-beach/ - fetched directly: 'Michael James, the Victorian representative on the Australian Naturist Federation, said...' and 'James, who has been going to Sunnyside North for about 30 years...'; contrast with F26 (SBS, Dec 2022) which attributes the 'emotional' quote and campaign leadership to 'Michael' with no surname given.
blocking.fix: Replace with: 'As of October 2023, a long-time regular was reporting, on the record, that none of the promised upgrades had shown up' - dropping the claim that this person organized the online campaign, matching showcase.json's safer phrasing.

blocking.claim: Do not confuse this with Southside Beach near Point Addis, 176 km away - a similarly named beach that itself replaced a nude beach whose legal status had been revoked, the real precedent for what a 'no' from the minister looks like.
blocking.problem: The '176 km' figure is misattributed. Per the ledger/fact sheet, F14 sources '176 kilometres each way' specifically to Point Impossible near Torquay ('the next closest is pt impossible near torquay and is 176 kilometres each way from sunnyside north'), not to Southside Beach near Point Addis. No fact in the sheet gives a sourced distance for Southside Beach. The page (correctly, elsewhere in key_facts and travel.mdx) attributes 176 km to Point Impossible; this margin note wrongly reassigns the same number to a different beach.
blocking.evidence: research/sunnyside-beach-3.json F14 (MPNews Oct 2023): '176 kilometres each way' is stated only about Point Impossible; F43 (Wikipedia: Southside Beach) gives no distance figure at all.
blocking.fix: Delete '176 km away' from the Southside Beach margin note (e.g. 'Do not confuse this with Southside Beach near Point Addis - a similarly named beach that itself replaced a nude beach whose legal status had been revoked...'), since no source in the sheet supports a distance figure for Southside.
